name: Разрез вклада мухи по условиям съёмки (ночь, пересвет, погода — атрибуты BDD)
essence: Break the fly's measured contributions down by the capture conditions that BDD100K labels per video (timeofday, weather, scene), plus a pixel-level overexposure measure. BDD labels only weather, timeofday and scene, so overexposure has to come from pixels. The contributions are: fly over its own input, fly over geometry, intact vs rewired connectome, and appearance over geometry. The aim is to replace 'the fly helps more at night' with a tested interaction (night minus day, with a CI) and to see whether overexposure or bad weather behaves like night. This is pure re-analysis: the per-video AP of every head is already stored, so a breakdown costs minutes of CPU and needs no new run.
sources: BDD100K: Yu et al., 'BDD100K: A Diverse Driving Dataset for Heterogeneous Multitask Learning', CVPR 2020. Frame attributes weather/scene/timeofday are in bdd100k_labels_images_{train,val}.json and are joined to MOT video ids by name (local: data/bdd100k/labels). Condition-stratified MOT evaluations since 2024: Kirillova, Mirza, Possegger, Bischof, 'Into the Fog: Evaluating Multiple Object Tracking Robustness', arXiv 2404.10534 (2024). Wang et al., 'Multi-Object Tracking in the Dark' (LMOT/LTrack), CVPR 2024, arXiv 2405.06600, code https://github.com/xinzwang/LMOT. Mancusi et al., 'Is Multiple Object Tracking a Matter of Specialization?' (PASTA), NeurIPS 2024: per-attribute experts, including lighting, merged in parameter space. Lee & Waslander, UncertaintyTrack, ICRA 2024 (BDD100K). Lappalainen et al., Nature 2024 (FlyVis). Project artifacts: runs/fly_reid_controls/report.json (per-video AP, dev_by_video/test_by_video), runs/fly_reid_controls/strata_bootstrap.json, runs/motion_reliability_lamina/strata_bootstrap.json and luminance.json, runs/fly_reid_null/compare.json, runs/train_cache/selection.json, scripts/build_overexposed_subset.py, experiments/results/overexposed_videos.json (30 val videos).
relevance: The thesis title names overexposure, low light, occlusion and complex background, yet the fly results are reported only as aggregates plus a dark/bright luminance split. The breakdown answers directly whether any fly benefit is specific to the adverse conditions in the title (registry N9 'input out of distribution at night'; night drop). It also guards against over-claiming: the 'twice as large at night' statement (+0.0102 dark vs +0.0054 bright) is two separate CIs, not a tested difference. Computed now from existing per-video AP in dev+test (70 videos, BDD timeofday joined from bdd100k_labels_images_train.json): the night-minus-day difference of (input + fly) - input is +0.0041 AP, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0032; +0.0117], so it is not significant. For appearance - geometry, night minus day is -0.057 [-0.123; +0.008]: appearance loses about a quarter of its gain at night, but this too is not significant. BDD timeofday and the project luminance threshold agree almost exactly: 27 of 29 night videos are < 60/255, and none of the 37 day or 4 dawn/dusk videos are.
novelty_overlap: Stratifying tracking results by BDD attributes or by synthetic degradation is routine (BDD100K paper; Into the Fog 2024; LMOT 2024; PASTA 2024 trains lighting-specific experts). Nobody stratifies a FlyVis/connectome descriptor by capture condition; [uncertain] Kuklev arXiv 2609.24565 works on engineering drawings, where the notion does not apply. cannot_claim: condition-stratified evaluation as a method, and 'first overexposure analysis' (novelty must not be argued from missing publications). Claimable: the measured night/day/weather profile of the fly's increment on BDD100K, with the same-information control, as an empirical result.
author_results: Into the Fog (MOT17 with physics-based fog at 4 levels, 30 fps, partly moving camera): under homogeneous fog, HOTA drops at levels 3/4 are ByteTrack 25%/67%, FairMOT 48%/83%, CenterTrack 51%/81%, Tracktor++ 71%/86%. Detection is the main bottleneck and re-ID features help only secondarily. LMOT (CVPR 2024; 32 RAW videos, 35,120 frames, dual camera with aligned well-lit/low-light pairs): with ByteTrack on LMOT, trained on all images, HOTA 28.1 vs 29.4 for LTrack; a low-light enhancement front end reaches at most 29.1 (SDSD), and LLFlow gives 28.8 at about 11x the FLOPs; on LMOT-real with OC-SORT, 34.6 vs 35.1. With ground-truth boxes on the LMOT validation set, appearance-only association falls from HOTA 87.3 / AssA 77.1 in well-lit to 53.8 / 32.1 in low light, while motion + appearance stays at 83.4 in low light. [uncertain] This row mapping is read from extracted PDF text. PASTA (NeurIPS 2024, MOTSynth, zero-shot to MOT17 and PersonPath22): merging attribute-specific PEFT experts selected per scene attribute beats the monolithic tracker. UncertaintyTrack (BDD100K MOT, 5 Hz): about -19% IDSw and +2-3% mMOTA overall; [uncertain] whether it reports a per-condition breakdown was not checked. A public GitHub project (PedramNikfajam/Traffic-Vision, not peer-reviewed) reports BDD MOTA 0.768 day, 0.485 night, 0.406 dawn/dusk.
measured_level: Authors: HOTA/MOTA/IDF1 after full tracking (Into the Fog, LMOT, PASTA). The project breakdown so far is at pair AP (re-ID pairs 'track ends -> another starts <= 2 s nearby'). HOTA per condition could be taken from existing TrackEval per-video outputs of the stitching runs (runs/fly_reid_ablation/stitch) without new tracking.
matched_control: Authors: none uses a same-information control. Project: every stratum can use the existing controls. Computed per BDD stratum from runs/fly_reid_controls/report.json (dev+test, per-video paired differences, bootstrap 5000). (input + fly) - input: night +0.0100 [+0.0036; +0.0171], 21 better / 7 worse; day +0.0060 [+0.0027; +0.0092], 28/9; dawn/dusk (n=4) -0.0007 [-0.0126; +0.0114]; rain+snow (n=6) +0.0093 [+0.0030; +0.0150], 5/1; overcast/partly cloudy (n=17) +0.0057 [+0.0007; +0.0110]; clear (n=38) +0.0084 [+0.0030; +0.0144]; city street (n=45) +0.0104 [+0.0065; +0.0150], 36/9; highway (n=17) +0.0006 [-0.0068; +0.0068], 9/7; residential (n=8) +0.0039 [-0.0025; +0.0107]. Fly - shuffled fly (on top of geometry) is roughly constant: night +0.1105, day +0.1111, highway +0.0585, city +0.1263. On top of geometry + appearance + input, the fly gives night +0.0055 [+0.0001; +0.0111] and day +0.0026 [+0.0002; +0.0052]. Connectome null by luminance (runs/fly_reid_null/compare.json): geometry + fly, intact - null, dark +0.0497 [+0.0264; +0.0744], bright +0.0391 [+0.0265; +0.0509]. [uncertain] All these strata are exploratory: they were not pre-registered, many comparisons were made, and no multiplicity correction was applied.
conditions_breakdown: Yes, and cheaply. Night/day comes from BDD timeofday (dev+test: night 29, day 37, dawn/dusk 4). Weather: clear 38, overcast 14, partly cloudy 3, rainy 3, snowy 3, undefined 9. Scene: city 45, highway 17, residential 8. Luminance strata already exist (dark 27 / bright 43, threshold 60/255). Missing: overexposure. BDD has no such attribute and the project's 30-video overexposed subset (experiments/results/overexposed_videos.json) comes from the val split, not from the 200 train-split videos used for the fly signatures. A saturated-pixel fraction (> 250/255, as in scripts/build_overexposed_subset.py) would need to be computed on the 70 dev+test videos. The train split (130 videos: 60 night, 11 snowy, 5 rainy) is larger but serves for fitting.
cost_here: CPU only; no GPU and no new signatures. Attribute join: one streaming pass over the 1.45 GB bdd100k_labels_images_train.json, about 1-2 min; all 200 selected videos are covered. Stratified paired bootstrap on existing per-video AP: seconds. Overexposure score on the 70 dev+test videos: decode about 12 sampled frames per video, a few minutes. Per-condition HOTA: re-read the TrackEval per-video results of the existing stitching runs if they are stored per video; [uncertain] otherwise re-running TrackEval on the stored tracker outputs takes about 1 h CPU. Nothing depends on runs/train_cache* beyond the already-computed signatures in runs/fly_signatures.
expected_effect: Not an accuracy gain but a sharper claim. From the numbers above, expect: (a) the fly's increment over input is positive in most conditions, largest in city night, and near zero on highway (+0.0006, n=17). [uncertain] A plausible mechanism for highway is larger inter-frame displacement and small distant objects, which shrink the fovea's useful content. (b) The night vs day interaction is not significant at n=70 (+0.004 [-0.003; +0.012]); detecting a difference of about +0.004 AP would need roughly 3-4x more videos [uncertain]. (c) Rain/snow looks like night (+0.009), but with n=6 it is not evidence. (d) Appearance weakens at night (+0.155 vs +0.212 over geometry), consistent with LMOT's collapse of appearance-only association in low light, but milder, because BDD night is lit by street lamps and headlights. HOTA per condition: expect differences within CI, since the aggregate fly effect on HOTA is 0.
risks: (1) Multiple comparisons: about 10 strata x 5 contrasts; report them as exploratory, or pre-register one primary contrast (night - day of (input + fly) - input) with Holm/BH for the rest. (2) Strata overlap and are confounded (night and city; highway and speed; weather 'undefined' at night), so no causal reading. (3) Pooling dev and test for strata mixes the model-selection split (C chosen on dev) with the test split. The project's strata_bootstrap already does this; state it, or repeat on test only (14 night / 21 day). (4) BDD attributes are per keyframe label and are sometimes wrong or 'undefined'; the luminance threshold is an independent check (agreement 27/29 night). (5) Small n (dawn/dusk 4, rain/snow 6): no conclusions. (6) An overexposure subset built after looking at fly results would be post-hoc; fix the saturation threshold (250/255, as in the existing script) and the top-k rule first. (7) Do not transfer signs from strata to aggregate claims, and do not present a null interaction as novelty.
attribution: Attributes: BDD100K (Yu et al. 2020). The practice of condition-stratified MOT evaluation: Into the Fog 2024, LMOT 2024, PASTA 2024. Ours: the stratified same-information and connectome-null analysis of the FlyVis fovea signature, the night-minus-day interaction test, and the pixel-level overexposure strata on the project's split.
